- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.5) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to avoid missing mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in correcting for sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from positive to negative, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecasts by reducing volatility-weighted variance in next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent peak, model overestimates; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent high if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment is low and price is near recent low, model underestimates; add 2–5% buffer to avoid missing bottoming out.
